summary: Peace studies scholar Topher L. McDougal explains how Israel's October 2023 halt on food, fuel and supply deliveries to Gaza threatens starvation in a territory already dependent on foreign aid after 16 years of blockade. He describes Gaza's weak, isolated economy, the central role of UNRWA in providing education, health care and shelter, and the fluctuating U.S. funding of that agency. He notes that aid groups and EU officials are calling for a humanitarian corridor, with no clear plans yet.
one_line: Israel's October 2023 halt on food and fuel deliveries to aid-dependent Gaza, after a 16-year blockade, raises starvation risk and strains UNRWA.
key_facts: Israel stopped allowing deliveries of food, fuel and other supplies to Gaza's 2.3 million residents on Oct. 10, 2023.
On Oct. 12, 2023, Israel warned 1.1 million Gaza residents in the northern section to move south ahead of a potential ground invasion.
International aid groups provide food and support to about 63% of people in Gaza, and about 64% of people there are food insecure.

Israel set up permanent air, land and sea blockades around Gaza in 2007, one year after Hamas rose to political power; the 16-year blockade previously did not apply to food and fuel brought in by aid groups.
The West Bank and Gaza economies run a deficit of US$6.6 billion in losses each year, and more than 53% of Gaza residents were below the poverty line in 2020.
Food as a share of Gaza's imports has risen 50% since 2005, while food production in the West Bank and Gaza has fallen 30%.
Israeli airstrikes hit Gaza's only power generation plant and main sewage treatment plant in 2008 and 2018, spreading sewage that destroyed farmland and threatened fish stocks.
UNRWA is the second-largest employer in Gaza after Hamas, running 284 schools educating over 294,000 children and 22 hospitals with 3.3 million patient visits per year.
Over 330,000 people in Gaza were displaced as of Oct. 12, 2023, and over two-thirds of them are staying in UNRWA schools.
The U.S. gave more than $500 million to Palestinians from April 2021 through March 2022, including more than $417 million to UNRWA.
In 2018 the Trump Administration cut roughly 30% of UNRWA's total budget in U.S. funding; the Biden administration restored it in 2021.
Since Oct. 8, more than 1,500 Gazans have been killed and more than 5,300 injured, while Hamas attacks killed more than 1,300 people in Israel.
Aid groups and European Union officials have called for a humanitarian corridor, but there are no clear plans for one.
